clue.text: Show how old you are in huff and puff

indicators.note: the age phrase is placed inside the breathing word, so 'in' signals a container

parts.note: to huff and puff is to pant
how old you are is your age

explanation.surface: A child is told to say their age between gasps of breath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show' looks like a verb (show your age) but is the noun definition; 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A pageant is a grand public spectacle or procession, a kind of show.

clue.text: Holy Joe finding boy substandard

parts.note: read as 'sub standard': the standard (par) sits above, the boy beneath it
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a lad is not up to scratch.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'substandard' as 'sub' (under) plus 'standard' (PAR): in this down clue SON goes under PAR. 'Holy Joe' is an informal name for a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: Holy Joe is slang for a clergyman or pious person, and a parson is a parish clergyman.

clue.text: Stuff full of energy to establish past entertainer

indicators.note: the gorging word holds the energy letter inside it, so 'full of' signals a container

parts.note: to stuff oneself is to gorge
E is the physics symbol for energy
to form something is to establish it
by can mean past, as in walking by

explanation.surface: A feast powers the founding of a show business career of old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'full of' puts E inside GORGE. GEORGE FORMBY was a British comic singer and ukulele player of the 1930s and 40s.
explanation.definitionFit: The ukulele-playing comedian was a famous music-hall and film entertainer of the past.

clue.text: Worker in Arab territory, one imprisoned as heretic

parts.note: the worker ant is the crossword's stock worker

indicators.note: the Arab country locks the numeral one inside it, so 'imprisoned' signals a container

parts.note: Oman is a sultanate on the Arabian peninsula
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A labourer in the Gulf is jailed for heresy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imprisoned' puts I inside OMAN to give OMIAN; 'in' is used literally.
explanation.definitionFit: An antinomian rejects moral law as binding on Christians, a view condemned as heresy.

clue.text: Book to raise hearts, perhaps, over time

indicators.note: the turned card word goes over and around the time letter, enclosing it
in a down clue, raising a word reads it from the bottom up, backwards

parts.note: hearts is one suit of cards

explanation.surface: A book meant to lift the spirits, given time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raise' turns SUIT into TIUS, and 'over' wraps it round T.
explanation.definitionFit: Titus is a book of the New Testament, one of Paul's pastoral epistles.

clue.text: Stupid person has half of beer after wine

indicators.note: the beer piece comes after the wine piece in the answer

parts.note: plonk is British slang for cheap wine

indicators.note: only the second half of the word for the drink is kept, its first two letters dropped

parts.note: taken as the word beer

explanation.surface: A fool drinks beer on top of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' keeps the second half of BEER. Plonk is British slang for cheap wine, and a plonker is a British insult.
explanation.definitionFit: Plonker is British slang for a foolish or inept person.

clue.text: Mums and dads are not welcomed by attendant

indicators.note: the contraction is taken in by the attendant, so 'welcomed by' signals a container

parts.note: a page is a young attendant
are not contracts to aren't

explanation.surface: Parents are left unwelcomed by a servant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mums and dads' is a playful plural definition for one's parents collectively; 'welcomed by' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Parentage means one's parents collectively, or descent from them.

clue.text: Token females leader brought out

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for females is taken away

parts.note: women are females

explanation.surface: A token gesture as women's leader is ousted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader brought out' removes the W from WOMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a sign or token of what is to come.

clue.text: Smart-arses ultimately crack with total lack of defence

indicators.note: only the final letter of crack is used

parts.note: with no walls a town has no defence

explanation.surface: Clever clogs finally crack when completely undefended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives K, the last letter of 'crack'.
explanation.definitionFit: Know-alls are irritating people who think they know everything, the same as smart-arses.

clue.text: Ultimately Boaz wasn't so unmerciful

definitions.meaning: in the Bible Boaz married Ruth, so in the end he was not without her

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the answer as RUTH-LESS: Boaz ended up with Ruth as his wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruthless means having no pity, the same as unmerciful.

clue.text: Beast in Oz given stone shelter

parts.note: a roo, short for kangaroo, is an Australian beast
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight

explanation.surface: A kangaroo is given a rocky refuge.
explanation.walkthrough: Oz is slang for Australia; ST abbreviates the stone, a British weight of 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A roost is a perch or place where birds shelter and rest.

clue.text: A tune to induce a grin could be what you got from 2 19

indicators.note: the clue words could be rearranged into something else, so 'could be' signals an anagram

parts.words: A tune to induce a grin

explanation.surface: A cheery song may bring out a smile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges all of A TUNE TO INDUCE A GRIN. The phrase was the catchphrase of the entertainer at 2 19.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase was the comedian's famous catchphrase, so it is what audiences got from him.

clue.text: Setting up something for accompanist, I give musical performance

parts.note: an organ is an instrument an accompanist plays
to sing is to give a musical performance

explanation.surface: An accompanist arranges a recital and performs.
explanation.definitionFit: Organising means arranging or setting up an event.

clue.text: Cloak to lose colour

definitions.meaning: a cloth or mantle covering something, such as a coffin
to become dull or lose its appeal

explanation.definitionFit: Pall is both a covering cloak and a verb for growing dull or losing interest.

clue.text: Fabric — everybody gets ragged bits to start with

indicators.note: the ragged bits come first, before the everybody piece

parts.note: tatters are ragged shreds of cloth
all means everybody

explanation.surface: Everyone receives scraps of cloth to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to start with' puts TATTERS first.
explanation.definitionFit: Tattersall is a checked fabric named after the London horse market where it was used on blankets.

clue.text: Mum's brought in song — summon singer

indicators.note: the song and summons are brought into mother's possessive

parts.note: Ma is mum, so Ma's is mum's
an aria is an operatic song
to call is to summon

explanation.surface: Mother's song is introduced as she calls on a singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought in' splits MA'S after its M; Maria Callas was the great soprano, so 'singer' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Maria Callas was a celebrated Greek-American operatic soprano.

clue.text: What one could do to stop binge drinking in principle?

parts.words: What one could do to stop binge
parts.note: rationing limits supply, preventing a binge
ale is something for drinking

explanation.surface: A suggestion for curbing heavy drinking, in theory.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the whole as RATION ALE, a cure for binge drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the underlying reason or principle behind something.

clue.text: The chap ran carelessly into car — drunken star

indicators.note: the chap and his run go into the reshuffled car
a drunken car weaves about, so its letters are scrambled

parts.note: he is the chap

indicators.note: running carelessly mixes up the letters of ran

explanation.surface: A man runs carelessly into a car, driven by a drunk who is seeing stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carelessly' gives RNA, 'drunken' gives ACR, and 'into' puts HE plus RNA inside ACR. Achernar is a bright star in Eridanus.
explanation.definitionFit: Achernar is the brightest star in the constellation Eridanus.

clue.text: Income to change? One may show happy face

indicators.note: the clue tells these letters to change, an instruction to rearrange them

explanation.surface: A pay change might bring a smile to someone's face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges INCOME TO; the question mark makes the definition a fair example rather than a strict synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: An emoticon is a typed symbol, like a smiley, that shows a facial expression.

clue.text: Remark about trick having to be withdrawn in the chamber

indicators.note: the remark goes round the turned trick, so 'about' signals a container

parts.note: a comment is a remark

indicators.note: withdrawing pulls the word backwards, reading it in reverse

parts.note: a trap is a trick

explanation.surface: Someone is told to withdraw a comment about a trick made in the debating chamber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be withdrawn' turns the trick word into PART; 'about' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A compartment is a separate section or chamber within a larger space.

clue.text: See 2
Hidden under sleeping place there's a big gun

indicators.note: in this down clue the letter goes beneath the sleeping place

parts.note: a berth is a bunk or sleeping place

explanation.surface: A large weapon is stowed under a bunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hidden under' places A below BERTH in the down entry. Big Bertha was a huge German howitzer of the First World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Big Bertha was the name of a giant German siege gun, so Bertha names a big gun.

clue.text: Creatures in multiloquent sessions

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of those two words

explanation.surface: Animals turn up at long-winded meetings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the answer as lying across 'multiloquENT Sessions'. Ents are tree-like creatures in Tolkien.
explanation.definitionFit: Ents are tree-giants in Tolkien's The Lord of the Rings, fantastic creatures.

clue.text: Club member

parts.note: the 'club' is the joking 'pudding club', slang for pregnancy, so its member is an expectant woman

explanation.walkthrough: 'In the pudding club' is British slang for being pregnant.
explanation.definitionFit: An expectant mother is jokingly a member of the pudding club, being pregnant.

clue.text: Fortune needed to secure an old goblet

indicators.note: the fortune word holds the article fast inside it

parts.note: hap is an old word for luck or fortune

explanation.surface: A fortune is needed to acquire an antique cup.
explanation.walkthrough: HAP is an archaic word for luck; 'to secure' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A hanap is a medieval ornate drinking goblet, often with a cover.

clue.text: Delay before duck gets into area liable to flood

indicators.note: the delay piece comes before the duck piece

parts.note: an interval or break in time can be a delay
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, so O

explanation.surface: A hold-up as a duck enters a marshy area.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a cricket score of zero, hence O. A gapó is seasonally flooded forest in the Amazon basin.
explanation.definitionFit: Gapo is forest land along Amazonian rivers flooded in the rainy season.

clue.text: See 10
Show in commercial institution in America

parts.note: an ad is a commercial
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: An advert is shown in an American college.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit a visitor is to let or show them in.

clue.text: Author wants to pay to rescue English

parts.note: to ransom someone is to pay for their release

explanation.surface: A writer wants to pay for the release of an Englishman.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Ransome was the English author of Swallows and Amazons.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Ransome was an English children's author, best known for Swallows and Amazons.

clue.text: Friend meeting girl behind tree

parts.note: a pal is a friend
Myra is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A friend meets a girl behind a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The palmyra is a tall fan palm of tropical Asia, a type of tree.
